column3: With respect to the Troy Towne Center Mortgage Loan (1.3%), the largest tenant, Kohl’s, representing approximately 59.9% of the net rentable square footage, is the shopping center’s anchor tenant. Consequently, the third and fourth largest tenants, Dollar Tree and Shoe Carnival, respectively, representing an aggregate 12.0% of net rentable square footage at the Mortgaged Property, have co-tenancy provisions tied to Kohl’s and with respect to Shoe Carnival only, the Walmart Supercenter located adjacent to the Mortgaged Property. With respect to Dollar Tree, if Kohl’s ceases to operate its business in less than 50% of its current size (at the time of lease execution), Dollar Tree, has the right to (i) if such condition continues for 6 months, pay 50% of base rent and (ii) if such condition continues for 12 months, terminate their lease upon 30 days’ written notice. Shoe Carnival has the right to pay an “Alternate Rent” of 3.0% of gross receipts from sales (not to exceed 50% of base rent otherwise due), in the event that either Kohl’s or the Walmart Supercenter located adjacent to the Mortgaged Property cease to be open and operating at their respective premises and are not replaced by a national or regional retail tenant. If Shoe Carnival has paid Alternate Rent for 18 months, Shoe Carnival has the option to terminate its lease upon 10 days’ written notice with the termination effective 60 days after receipt thereof. In 2025, Kohl’s announced the closure of 27 underperforming stores throughout the United States, two of which were located in Ohio.
